subject: Using INLA with arbitrary link functions

messages.author: 9b16b466bc328f83
messages.subject: Using INLA with arbitrary link functions
parts:
Hello,

I wanted to know if its possible to use INLA with an arbitrary (but smooth) link function - either as it is currently or through minor modifications of its code base ? Also, are there any theoretical restriction on the link function ?

Our group has been developing methods for finite element (FE) simulations of tissue models from imaging data - for e.g. using FE models to align two brain images acquired pre and intra-operatively with MRI. As part of this, we have been exploring techniques to characterize the posterior distributions of the FE-mesh deformations conditioned on imaging data and various imaging parameters, in order to understand their effect on the uncertainty of the models. FE-meshes exhibit Markov structure, where the effect of a deformation at one mesh vertex is restricted to only a very small neighborhood. Moreover, assuming elastic material properties, the total deformation energy of the mesh has a quadratic form, which provides a Gaussian prior distribution on mesh deformation parameters. As a result, the model takes on a GMRF form with only linear dependance on its parameters modulated through the link function  - and therefore we were interested in using INLA to study these posterior distributions. However, the link function g is the image that maps a voxel location in R^3 to R.

We would really appreciate any suggestions on how to proceed.

Thanks,
-firdaus

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: Using INLA with arbitrary link functions
parts:
Wow! This sounds like a really interesting application!

In principle, it is not difficult to add a link function to INLA and if you have a specific form, we can probably add it for you fairly quickly.  

There is one fairly important caveat: If the link function isn't monotone, there's no guarantee that pi(x|y,\theta) will be unimodal and so the Laplace approximation (as implemented) may not work very well!  In theory, every Laplace approximation could be computed as a mixture of a Gaussian approximation at each mode, however this is not handled (and will probably not be handled in the future) by our INLA code.

Hope this helps,

Dan
